brief: The Market Ear argues NDX's bounce is failing: the index was rejected at its 200-day moving average and is still above recent panic lows but with weak momentum, making 27,000 in NDX futures (last autumn's pivot and the site of the long-term trendline) the key level, whose loss would open further downside. Equity volatility is spiking again with the VXN-VIX gap unusually wide. Goldman says momentum traders are near maximum short in NDX and that CTAs sold over $22bn of S&P 500 exposure in the past week; elevated realized volatility is forcing systematic funds broadly to cut risk, with vol control and risk parity strategies estimated to have sold over $30bn combined over the week, though Goldman flags these funds could start re-risking in December/January if volatility settles, a potential equity tailwind. Deutsche Bank notes discretionary investors added exposure from the bottom of the range even as systematic strategies kept cutting, while net call volume and bullish options strategies sit at their lowest levels in a while. Goldman adds call skew stayed dead through the recent squeeze, even before the reversal lower, so the options market never bought into the bounce.
